digest.component_or_area: reconciler bridge state cache and tickets repository storage
propositions: The reconciler's committed `.bridge_state` cache is 92% of the 1.04 GiB tickets branch size and grows wastefully due to bookkeeping fields `baseline_advanced_at` and `last_get_pass` that are written frequently but read never or rarely.
Packed marginal cost per `bindings.json` version is 12.79 KB today; eliminating the timestamp reduces it 7.4x to 1.74 KB and moving rotation bookkeeping reduces total churn 12.8x.

The cache must remain committed on-branch because the reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub runners and requires durable state in git; the solution is to reduce content and churn, not relocate the cache.

A one-time history rewrite using `git fast-export | filter | git-import` can reclaim ~1 GiB by removing historical versions of target paths while preserving all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges; the rewritten HEAD tree is byte-identical to the pre-rewrite tip after dynamic re-add.

Rollout requires mixed-version read/write compatibility: A2-1 continues legacy writes, A2-2 stops legacy writes but reads `max(new, legacy)`, A4-2 requires forward and reverse corpus diffs, and A6-0a adds epoch guards at union sites before reclaim publication.

Post-reclaim rollback is operator-controlled via off-repo bundle restore and mandatory writer re-clone on epoch mismatch; the process requires quiescence confirmation, in-flight workflow disable verification, and fail-closed epoch refusal in live clients.
